title: SNT_metadata.json (shape of 2026-09-08)
description: Declares the data layers the SNT Explorer offers to a user, for one country. Each top-level property is one layer: SOURCE_DATA says where its values come from, the remaining fields say how it is presented. Work in progress — being validated with the IASO developers. Rationale, conventions and open questions: docs/schemas/README.md.

propertyNames.description: The layer id. UPPER_SNAKE_CASE, unique within the file, and stable once published — the Explorer and any saved user selection refer to a layer by this id. It is NOT required to equal SOURCE_DATA.COLUMN: two layers may read the same column from different files (see REPORTING_RATE_DATAELEMENT and REPORTING_RATE_DATASET in the example).

upperSnakeName.description: UPPER_SNAKE_CASE identifier: starts with a letter, no leading/trailing/double underscores.

localizedText.description: The same text in each supported language. Both keys are required so a missing translation is visible as an empty string rather than an absent key. An empty string means 'not translated yet' — how the Explorer renders that is an OPEN QUESTION (see README, Open questions #1).

EN.description: English. May be "" if not yet translated.

FR.description: French. May be "" if not yet translated.

layer.description: One data layer: where to read it, and how to present it.

LABEL.description: Short name shown in the Explorer's layer list and map legend. Keep it short enough to fit a legend; put the detail in DESCRIPTION. House style is to end with the source in parentheses, e.g. "Crude incidence (DHIS2)".

DESCRIPTION.description: One or two sentences defining the indicator for a non-technical reader: what is counted, over what population, with what adjustment. Shown on hover / in the layer's info panel.

SOURCE.description: Origin of the data as shown to the user — e.g. "DHIS2", "DHS", "WorldPop", "ERA5". This is a display credit, not a machine reference: the machine-readable origin is SOURCE_DATA.DATASET.

UNITS.description: Unit of the values, spelled out for a human — e.g. "Per 1000 people", "Number of people", "Proportion". The short form for an axis or legend is UNIT_SYMBOL.

CATEGORY.description: The group the layer is filed under in the Explorer's layer list — e.g. "Epidemiological indicators", "Qualité des données". Layers sharing a category MUST spell it identically in every language, or they split into two groups in the UI. There is no controlled list yet (OPEN QUESTION: README, Open questions #3).

TYPE.description: How the Explorer turns values into map colours. "Threshold" = classify into bins whose cut points are SCALE. Only this value has been used so far; the enum is deliberately narrow so an unreviewed new value fails validation rather than reaching IASO unnoticed. Adding a rendering mode means adding it here AND agreeing it with the IASO developers (README, Open questions #4).

SCALE.description: Cut points between colour bins, ascending, in the units of the column. DO NOT include the outer limits (no leading 0, no trailing max) — the SNT Explorer adds those itself. So n values produce n+1 bins. Ascending order is a REQUIREMENT that JSON Schema cannot express; check it by eye or with the validator in README §Validating.

UNIT_SYMBOL.description: Short symbol appended to values in legends and tooltips, e.g. "%". null when the values carry no symbol (a count, or a rate already spelled out in UNITS). Must agree with how SCALE is expressed: "%" implies SCALE holds percentages (0-100), null with UNITS "Proportion" implies SCALE holds fractions (0-1). The example currently violates this and it is unresolved (README, Open questions #2).

sourceData.description: Where the layer's values are read from: one column, of one file, in one version of one OpenHEXA dataset. This block is what makes the file a machine-resolvable pointer rather than presentation metadata only.

DATASET.description: The OpenHEXA dataset holding the file.

NAME.description: MUST be a key of SNT_DATASET_IDENTIFIERS in the country's SNT_config.json — that is how the SNT Explorer resolves the layer to a real dataset, by looking the key up to get the workspace dataset identifier (e.g. DHIS2_INCIDENCE -> "snt-dhis2-incidence"). Write the CONFIG KEY here, not the dataset's display name in the OpenHEXA UI and not its slug. A key absent from the config resolves to nothing and the layer fails to load. Not enumerated in this schema because the valid set lives in the per-country config; cross-check it with the validator in README section 5.

VERSION.description: Which dataset version to read. "latest" follows the newest version — the only value used so far, and the one that makes a re-run pick up fresh data automatically. A pinned version id would make a published Explorer view reproducible; whether IASO supports that is an OPEN QUESTION (README, Open questions #6).

FILENAME.description: File within that dataset. MUST begin with the literal placeholder {COUNTRY_CODE}, which the consumer substitutes with the uppercase country code from SNT_CONFIG.COUNTRY_CODE — this is what lets one metadata file serve every country (repo rule R7: every data file is prefixed {CC}_). Keeping the placeholder literal, rather than writing "COD_incidence.csv", is deliberate: a hardcoded code silently reads the wrong country's file if the config is copied.

COLUMN.description: Column within that file holding the layer's values. UPPERCASE, per repo rule R10 (all published column names are uppercase). Need not be unique across the file — the layer id is what disambiguates.
